get.description:
Push monitors: `status` is `up` (the default) or `down`; a reported down skips the retries. `msg` is
stored as the result message (longer than 200 characters is cut). `ping` is the latency in
milliseconds; anything but a non-negative integer is ignored. Cron monitors: records the run as up,
with the time since its start as latency.
get.summary: Report a heartbeat or a successful cron run

get.description: Records a down that skips the retries, with `msg` appended to the message when given.
Records nothing; the run's duration is measured from here and its maximum runtime is enforced.
get.summary: Report that a cron run has started

get.description: Exit code 0 records the run as up; 1 to 255 record a down that skips the retries.
get.summary: Report a finished cron run by its exit code

post.summary:
Complete the first-run setup. Must be called as a stateful (cookie) request: send an `Origin` that
matches `APP_URL` and the `X-XSRF-TOKEN` obtained from `GET /sanctum/csrf-cookie`

get.description:
`actor_user_id` is the person behind the action: the user for session actors and the owner of the
token for token actors; it is null for system actions.
get.summary: List audit events of the workspace, newest first. Filters: `action`, `actor_id`, `actor_type`, `actor_user_id`
List the monitor's events (status changes and changes of watched values), newest first. Filter: `kind`

List the monitor's raw check results, newest first. Raw results are kept for `RETENTION_RAW_HOURS`.
Filters: `from`, `to` (ISO 8601), `status`

List the monitor's rollups of one bucket size, oldest first. Day buckets start at midnight in the
workspace timezone. `availability` is (up + degraded + pending) / (total - maintenance), or null when
every check fell into maintenance. Filters: `bucket` (required), `from`, `to` (ISO 8601, applied to the
bucket start)
